Claim: session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8395-copyfield-object-values`

PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and never writes the assignee field.

**Unblocked:** objectui#8376 / PR #8396 has landed (`hasCellValue` now in `DetailSection.tsx`), so the file is free. ⚠️ Re-derive the line — it moved.

The defect is crisp: `handleCopyField` writes `String(value)`, so click-to-copy puts the literal text `[object Object]` on the clipboard for every object-valued cell (address, geolocation, JSON, attachment, multiselect, expanded lookup) — **while the cell beside the button renders that same value correctly**.

⚠️ That asymmetry is the design constraint, not just the symptom: **the cell already knows how to turn the value into text, and the copy button does not ask it.** Before writing a serializer of your own, measure whether the rendered text is reachable — copying what the user can actually see is a different and better contract than copying a re-derivation that can drift from it. If it is not reachable, say so and then propose.

⛔ **Escalation fence:** "what should copying an object cell put on the clipboard" is a product question wherever the answer is not simply *the text on screen* — a JSON blob, a formatted address, a lat/long pair and an attachment filename are four different answers. If the measurement does not hand you one obvious contract, **report the options costed and stop**.

The pin must assert **the clipboard payload**, with a control proving the cell rendered its value — an assertion that the payload is not `[object Object]` passes on a cell that copied nothing.

PM ruling — **C**, and the measurement is accepted as falsifying my own brief.

## My brief was wrong, and your measurement is why

I wrote: *"Copying what the user can actually see is a different and better contract than copying a re-derivation that can drift from it."* Measured, that is **the worse contract for 9 of 17 field types**, and two of them lose data silently:

```
date      RENDERED 'Mar 4'              → the YEAR is gone   (today '2026-03-04')
percent   RENDERED '12%'   stored 0.123 → a DIFFERENT QUANTITY
datetime  RENDERED '3/4/20265:06 am'    → unparseable
currency  '1,234.50' · number '16.00'   → break spreadsheet paste
image ''  ·  boolean ''                 → the empty string
files '2 files' · repeater '2 项'        → a COUNT, not the data
multiselect 'AlphaBeta'                 → today's 'alpha,beta' is strictly better
```

⭐ And the sharpest part: **option A reaches the "strictly worse than the bug" implementation my own brief told you to watch for, by following my own brief** — image and boolean cells would copy `''`. That is the second time today a dispatch's specified shape would have been satisfied by something worse than the defect, and the first time the shape was mine rather than the card's.

Your framing settles it: A trades **a loud bug** (a reader pastes `[object Object]` and knows instantly) for **a quiet one** (a reader pastes `Mar 4` and never learns the year was dropped).

Also noted: the one cost the issue body named — truncation — **is not real** (`TruncatedText` truncates in CSS, so `textContent` is complete), and A would additionally make the clipboard payload **display-locale dependent**, which no one asked for.

## Ruling: ship C now, B is a separate card

**C** — keep `String(value)` for non-objects, `JSON.stringify` for objects. It is the only option that **cannot make anything worse than today**: it touches only the broken branch, leaves all five correct-today scalar payloads byte-identical, and needs no DOM read and no locale coupling.

Yes, C answers "what should an object cell copy" by fiat with *a JSON blob*. That is a **defensible default, not a settled contract**, and the PR must say so at the read site — so that whoever takes B is not misled into thinking the question was decided. Cheapest to ship, cheapest to change.

**B** is the right long-term shape and it is a **separate, properly specified card** — it requires per-kind product answers (address under which locale, geolocation at stored precision or displayed rounding, json compact or pretty, file filename/list/URL, multiselect labels or values, lookup name or id, image URL or filename), and those answers do not exist yet.

**D** stays out: narrowing `canCopy` away from `hasCellValue` contradicts objectui#8376's docblock that the three readers of that definition must agree. Correctly identified as belonging to that card's owner.

## Your process question — answered

You are right that my dispatch carried **no decision frame**, and right not to invent axes. For this card: **measured cost is the whole basis I want**, and your report supplies it. Going forward I will send an explicit frame on any card whose fence I expect to fire, rather than leaving you to choose between inventing axes and reporting bare costs.

## Your two filed cards

objectui#8440 (copy writes a secret's raw value while the cell renders the mask) and objectui#8441 (the hardcoded `2 项`) are both accepted and labelled. objectui#8440 is **not** folded into C — it is the same handler but a different branch and, as you note, its own decision; it goes to the maintainer box because both available answers (copy the mask / withdraw the affordance) have a real cost, the second one being the same `canCopy`-vs-`hasCellValue` constraint that rules D out here.

The `FileCellRenderer` `'N files'` note folded into objectui#8441 is the right call — a third near-duplicate card would have been noise.

Re-dispatching this card as C now.
